newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 13.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Staples agreed to sell 63 stores to OfficeMax in an effort to avoid a federal antitrust challenge to its proposed $4 billion acquisition of Office Depot.
* The Dow Jones Industrial Average is adding Travelers Group, Hewlett-Packard, Johnson & Johnson and Wal-Mart and dropping Westinghouse, Texaco, Bethlehem Steel and Woolworth.
* A recent federal survey shows that labor shortages are rising, but companies aren't offering higher salaries.
* Volkswagon's Audi is planning to spend up to $780 million to build a new production plant in the South.
* General Motors released a financial breakdown of its auto-building operations and its Delphi auto parts unit in preparation for the public sale of 20 percent of Delphi.
* Marsh & McLennan's stock rose 5.7 percent after it revealed an agreement to acquire Johnson & Higgins for $1.8 billion in cash and stock.
* Eugene Lockhart resigned as president and chief executive of MasterCard International to take a job as head of retail banking at BankAmerica.
* General Electric Chairman and Chief Executive John Welch received $6.3 million in pay in 1996 plus $15.1 million under a long-term incentive plan.
* The Dow industrials dropped 45.79 to 7,039.37. Bond prices also fell and the dollar was mixed.
* A federal grand jury indicted Emanuel Pinez, the former chief executive of Centennial Technologies, on five counts of securities fraud.
* Gerber promised to halt advertising claiming that doctors recommend its baby food after the Federal Trade Commission said such ads were deceptive.
* Sylvan Learning Systems agreed to acquire National Education Corp for about $641 million.
* Southwestern Bell agreed to become the sole distributor for Lucent's business products in its five-state region, cancelling its pact with Northern Telecom.
* New Jersey's highest court has upheld a $738,000 jury verdict against Borden Inc, a unit of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co, in a contract dispute involving the purchase of clams.

* What's behind the huge rally in cigarette stocks? One big reason: mounting speculation that a "magic bullet" legislative solution will wipe away the regulatory and legal attacks that have long dogged the cigarette makers and depressed their share prices.

But tobacco investors shouldn't necessarily wait to exhale. The odds are against a sweeping settlement that eliminates all the industry's liabilities and unites all the major cigarette companies, the White House, Congress, plaintiffs' lawyers, 50 state attorneys general and antismoking health activists. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bonds fell for the second consecutive day as investors, fearful of an interest-rate increase later this month, ignored an economic report describing a growing economy facing little inflationary pressure. -- Credit Markets.
